definition: A particle given out by some unstable nuclei, made of 2 protons and 2 neutrons (a helium nucleus), with a charge of $+2$; it is the most strongly ionising emission and a sheet of paper stops it.
A fast-moving electron given out by an unstable nucleus, with a charge of $-1$; it ionises less than an alpha particle and is stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium.

An electromagnetic wave given out by an unstable nucleus, with no charge and no mass; it is the least ionising and most penetrating emission, and several centimetres of lead reduce it without stopping it all.
How far a type of radiation can travel through a material before the material absorbs it.
